_annotation: Income toolkit at the market desk (T05). typeOptions/treatmentOptions are the TYPE and TREATMENT note cards (general rules only, never Rosa-specific). tutorial is T0, an unrelated fictional payslip the guide demonstrates once and the player repeats; it is never scored. entries (Rosa's E1-E4) and their separate answer keys arrive with T06.

typeOptions.label: Compensation income
typeOptions.rule: pay from an employer for work done as an employee.

typeOptions.label: Business / service income
typeOptions.rule: money earned from your own trade or from jobs done for customers.

typeOptions.label: Rental income
typeOptions.rule: money received for letting someone use your property.

typeOptions.label: Passive income (interest)
typeOptions.rule: earnings from money or investments, such as bank interest. Check its own rule before deciding its treatment.

typeOptions.label: Borrowed funds
typeOptions.rule: money that must be paid back. Borrowing is not earning.

treatmentOptions.label: Regular income schedule
treatmentOptions.rule: earned income listed with the other income for the period.

treatmentOptions.label: Separate rule
treatmentOptions.rule: some income follows its own rule instead of the regular schedule. Check that rule first.

treatmentOptions.label: Statutory exclusion
treatmentOptions.rule: only for items a law itself excludes. Use it only when a rule says so.

treatmentOptions.label: Not income
treatmentOptions.rule: money that was not earned, such as a loan that must be repaid.

evidenceOptions.label: Payslip PS-0430
evidenceOptions.rule: the record of this pay: who paid, for what work, and when.

evidenceOptions.label: Company ID card
evidenceOptions.rule: shows where someone works, not what they were paid.

evidenceOptions.label: Bank passbook page
evidenceOptions.rule: shows money arriving, not why it was paid.

demo.introLine: Before Rosa's records, let me show you once on someone else's payslip. It's practice: nothing here is scored.
demo.highlightLine: First, pick up the yellow highlighter. Aim at the line that shows the money and what it was paid for, then swipe across it.
demo.evidenceLine: Last, clip the record that proves it: the payslip itself.
demo.yourTurnLine: Your turn. Tap the highlighter to lift it beside the paper, then drag it onto the salary line and sweep across. Add TYPE and TREATMENT cards, then clip the payslip. Tap a card and its place, or drag it.
demo.doneLine: Practice complete: your highlight, TYPE, TREATMENT and evidence match. This build ends here; Rosa's record challenge is not available yet. Use Exit Desk to leave.

_annotationKey: Answer key for Mark the Money! (T06): one per entry, separate from the player-facing records. Hints go from a general rule to a specific one on later checks; they never mention summary totals, findings or the stamp.

typeHints: Customers pay Rosa for washing their clothes: money from her own trade.
Payments for her laundry work are Business / service income.
treatmentHints: Money earned from ordinary work goes with the other income of the period.
evidenceHints: Which one record lists these clothes-washing payments for the month?
Clip only the monthly collection sheet, D1.
highlightHints: Find the row that states the full payment for clothes-washing work.
Highlight the combined payment row, rather than a separate bank or cash entry.

typeHints: A guesthouse paid Rosa to do a washing job for them.
A paid job done for a customer is Business / service income.
treatmentHints: A paid job is earned money, like her other work.
evidenceHints: Which record was written for this job?
highlightHints: Find the amount paid for the washing job.
Highlight the amount row on the payment record.

typeHints: She was paid for letting someone use her machine.
Letting someone use your property earns Rental income.
treatmentHints: This is an ordinary rental with no special rule of its own.
evidenceHints: Which receipt shows the machine being rented?
highlightHints: Find the row showing how much Rosa received for letting someone use the machine.

typeHints: Rosa has to pay this money back.
Money that must be repaid is Borrowed funds.
treatmentHints: Use Not income: it is not an exclusion, it was never earned.
evidenceHints: One record shows the money arriving; another shows why it was paid.
Clip the bank statement D2 and the loan agreement D5 together.
highlightHints: A bank credit shows money arriving, but check the description before treating it as income.
Highlight the credit row so you can compare it with the loan record.

_office: Office reconciliation (T07). conclusions and the new reason are offered by the book. scheduleSources are the record lines the player may put in the reviewed schedule; moneyIds stop the same payment being counted twice. officeFindings are the F1 follow-up and the F2 comparison prompt (player-facing). officeRule is answer data for the evaluator (T09): never printed.

officeFindings.title: Finding F2 · Do two records disagree?

_finalAndAudit: T08 assessmentReasons (book offers them; verdict/names are answer meaning, labels are generic). T09 audit lines per outcome and per root cause (point to the record or rule, never fix it). T10 review cutoff clock (active seconds per day, warnings, one late consequence).

approved: Approved. Every income entry has a supported place, and the difference is explained.
audit.justifiedHold: You have a reason to hold this. Use the collected records to finish the unresolved item.
audit.prematureApproval: This isn't ready yet. Look at this before you approve it again.
audit.falseHold: The amounts cover different payment channels. Check the cash record before requesting more paperwork.
audit.reasonError: Your recommendation and its reason don't match what this review shows. Check the reason you chose.
audit.unchanged: Nothing has changed since I last looked. Change the review, stamp it again, then bring it back.
audit.rosaHold: Rosa: "Can this still be finished today? Tell me what you need."
audit.rosaPremature: Rosa: "I thought it was finished. Please tell me what still needs fixing."
audit.rosaFalseHold: Rosa: "I brought those receipts already. Can we use them to finish this?"

feedback.line: This payment still has no supported place in the summary. Check the record of the payment for a separate blanket-washing job.
An earned payment from Rosa's records is missing from your schedule. Check each record's money line.
Money that must be repaid is not earnings. Check the loan agreement before counting it.
Finding F1 needs the original record and a conclusion that matches what you changed.
Finding F2 doesn't explain the difference yet. Compare the collection sheet, the bank statement and the cash receipt.
One of Rosa's taxpayer facts on the first page needs another look.
